sources.citation: Klimiuk, Maciej (ed.). 2022. Semitic Dialects and Dialectology: Fieldwork-Community-Change. Heidelberg: Heidelberg University Publishing. doi:10.17885/heiup.859
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No chapter on Uzbekistan Arabic. Bozkurt's chapter on Arabkhane (South Khorasan, Iran; a Khorasan Arabic variety, not uzbe1248) notes that f.pl. verb/pronoun forms are 'endbetont' (final-stressed): citilan, citaltan, yicitban, intan. Not applicable to the target without identity caveat.

sources.citation: Chikovani, Guram. 2025. The Current Situation in Arabic-Speaking Kishlaks of Central Asia. In A. J. Frendo & K. Gatt (eds.), Arabic in Context: Essays in Honour of Martin R. Zammit (Semitic Languages and Cultures), 13-30. Cambridge: Open Book Publishers. doi:10.11647/OBP.0445.02
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic situation plus morphological/lexical notes on Bukhara (BAD) and Qashqa-Darya (QAD) dialects; the words stress/accent/syllable do not occur in the chapter (pp. 13-30). Its reference list confirms the primary grammars: Chikovani 2002 (Georgian), 2007 (Georgian texts), 2008 (Russian), 2022 (Tbilisi book).

sources.citation: Yushmanov, N. V. 1931. Arabskoe narechie sovetskogo vostoka. In B. Ya. Vladimirtsov (ed.), Kul'tura i pis'mennost' Vostoka, kn. X, 75-?. Moscow: VTsK NA.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Based on Burykina & Izmaylova's 1930 records from Jugary (Bukhara) and Jeynau (Qashqa-Darya). p. 78: 'Не отмечая количества и ударения, авторы записи лишают нас возможности дать определенное суждение о вокализме нашего наречия' (the recorders marked neither quantity nor stress, so no judgment on vocalism is possible); he only conjectures three vowel phonemes 'с различием по ударенности и неударенности'. No statement of stress placement.
